TLS certificates

There are two certificates in this system and they are not the same thing: one protects the panel in your browser, and one protects the panel's connection to each node.

The panel's certificate

A fresh install uses a self-signed certificate. The connection is genuinely encrypted; the browser just cannot tell who issued the certificate, so it warns once. Click Advanced, then Proceed. The installer's certificate carries the server's public IP as its common name and has no subject alternative names — that is deliberate, and the panel's health probe pins the file it reads rather than checking the hostname.

The panel serves HTTPS from the pair in .env, or from DATA_DIR/tls when no override is set. The matching command is the interactive ovmanager tls menu (status, remove, self-signed, custom install), not https.

Use your own certificate

In-process ACME issuance was removed. Put a browser-trusted certificate at DATA_DIR/tls/fullchain.pem and DATA_DIR/tls/privkey.pem (or point TlsCertFile/TlsKeyFile at them), then restart the panel. Any external client — certbot, acme.sh, your CA — can produce the pair. There is no renewal timer inside the panel.

The node's certificate

The node's sync API also serves TLS. The installer never offers plain HTTP — the API key travels in a header on every request. The panel verifies that certificate strictly first, and warns once per node when a self-signed fallback is forced.

The node's OpenVPN server certificate is a separate thing. The node generates and manages it; ovnode tls on the node shows and replaces it, and the panel reports its expiry through the sync API.

Watching for expiry

WhereWhat to look at
Panel, via ovmanager tlsInstalled certificate, source and expiry, with issue/renew/remove actions
Node, via ovnode tls statusNode sync API certificate (self-signed or Let's Encrypt) and remaining validity
Node, via ovnode statusOpenVPN server certificate expiry, refreshed per probe

TLS is terminated by the panel

The panel serves HTTPS itself. There is no reverse-proxy mode: forwarded headers are not trusted, the client IP is the peer address, and HSTS is emitted only on a real TLS connection. Point DNS at the panel and use TlsCertFile/TlsKeyFile (or the installer's TLS step) for the certificate.
